articles.title: Unregulated loan notes and mini-bonds: don't risk your savings on promises of high returns
articles.summary: These high-risk investments should not usually be advertised widely to the public. We banned the marketing of speculative mini-bonds and loan notes to ordinary retail investors from 1 January 2021.We did this because these are complicated investments, not suitable for most people. The ban means these high-risk investments should not usually be advertised widely to the public.But some unregulated firms may still try to sell them by using legal exemptions. You should be on alert if you’re offered these types of investments by someone not regulated by us. They may ask you to tick a box saying you are a sophisticated, experienced or high-net-worth investor before you can invest. Most people don’t meet these criteria.Be very careful before ticking any boxes, as it could mean you lose important protections if things go wrong. You’re unlikely to be able to take complaints to the Financial Ombudsman Service or make a claim through the Financial Services Compensation Scheme.

articles.title: How Banks and PSPs Can Ensure Innovation Without Excluding Vulnerable Adults
articles.summary: Joining the FinextraTV studio, Sean Tyrer, CEO and Founder, Money Carer helped to contextualise some of the key obstacles to traditional payments and banking that vulnerable adults face. Tyrer explains how, in the race to make payments faster, vulnerable adults are often left out of the equation, emphasising the need for optionality more than just assumed speed and innovation. He further describes how technologies like biometric cards and wearables are a strong way for banks and PSPs to continue evolving and innovating their offerings, while ensuring an inclusive product base.

articles.title: Misconception or Magic: What to Know About the Modern Wealth Management World
articles.summary: At the Communify Intelligence Experience, Rupert Baron, co-founder, TechnoWealth, returns to Finextra TV to unpack how the definition of wealth keeps moving and what that means for the industry. Baron argues the FCA's softening of the rules is nudging wealth management toward greater nuance rather than greater complexity, questions whether firms have truly embraced AI beyond the LLM, and reframes the great wealth transfer as a two-step process – first to the surviving spouse, statistically a woman, and only later to the next generation.

articles.title: Why Banks Should Invest in More Orchestration for Better Security
articles.summary: At EBAday 2026 in Copenhagen, Trevor LaFleche, Director, Global Banking Products, ACI Worldwide, spoke to FinextraTV about orchestration within Wero and other payment trends. LaFleche suggested that banks are still in a 'siloed mode' . LaFleche recommends that banks focus more on investing in that orchestration across platforms, mentionining fraud and AML checks are crucial services to be consistent across all areas.

articles.title: How to Define Relevant Metrics for a Successful Core Modernisation Project
articles.summary: Joining FinextraTV at the Temenos Community Forum 2026, Paul Weiss, Chief Transformation Officer, Regions Bank, discussed core modernisation and, crucially, how to actually measure its success. Weiss suggested starting with the reason that the transformation is necessary first, and finding clarity at that point in order to enable natural KPI's to follow. Weiss emphasised the need to see each journey as bank specific and not necessarily follow a set repeatable structure. When asked about lessons for other banks, he said they need to understand their total environment solution in order to proactively embed potential constraints into the timeline.

articles.title: How Technology Creates a Better Human Advisory Experience
articles.summary: Joining the FinextraTV virtual studio, Roshan Shetty, BFSI Public Sectors Head, Americas, Tech Mahindra and Bindhu Alvar Thiruvenkadathan, Chief Information Officer, Wealth Management, explained how the wealth management sector is currently adopting AI. Discussing the role of trust and security, they ultimately explain how technology is helping to provide humans with the individual customer details they need, faster. This technological intervention, they say, is built to match the customer needs that have outpaced advisor capabilities. Using this need for personalisation, and the capabilities of AI, they explain, actually ends up creating a deeper, human experience with advisors, by improving trust via speed and customisation.

articles.title: Different Rails for Different Purposes: The Nuance of Simplifying Modern Banking
articles.summary: At EBADay in Copenhagen, Craig Ramsey, Global Head of A2A Payments, ACI Worldwide joined the FinextraTV studio to discuss the changes in Instant Payments. Addressing growth, Ramsey said that initiatives like Wero are really taking off at speed and the crucial point now is ensuring that banks can still keep up with these changes and scale reliably. Ramsey described how different each rail looks, comparing ACH to Swift to Instant to RTGS and how each has different scales of complexities and the world, according to Ramsey, will only get more complex - it's banks job to simplify the offering.

articles.title: The Importance of Banking Through An Empathetic Lens
articles.summary: Joining FinextraTV at Temenos Community Forum, Muhammad Faisal Anwar, CTO, HBL discussed core modernisation and lessons learned along the journey. When thinking about whether core modernisation was 'just an IT problem, Anwar explained that banks falter when they don't first create a problem statement and what the core journey will solve. Equally, Anwar described the importance of empathy, explaining how employees should be regarded as ambassadors for the business, and how their satisfaction and morale are just as crucial. He went on to advise banks to see customer transactions as 'lifestyles' more than products or services - a house, a car, a holiday.

articles.title: What's the Right Level of Friction for Pay-by-Bank?
articles.summary: Joining FinextraTV at Payments Unleashed in London, Dean Wallace, Director, Consumer Payments Modernisation, ACI Worldwide discussed the evolution of pay-by-bank and some of the current obstacles. Wallace provided context to the growth, describing how many have tried to get rid of cards and pay-by-bank is perhaps the most succesful, but is still not an aggressive threat, given how ingrained cards still are. Looking at multi-rail environments, Wallace explains that the way that banks or cooperatives transition customers to new approaches and away from cards will define whether they stay loyal. He goes on to discuss the presence of friction and how some level allows a customer to feel safe, but too much will ruin the experience.

articles.title: What is the Real Asset Thesis for Investable Conservation?
articles.summary: Joining FinextraTV for an episode of Unplugged, Tripp Wall, Founder and CEO, Pantheon Regeneration and Managing Partner, Trailhead Capital discussed his light bulb moment that prompted a new asset thesis for investable conservation. Providing context into his journey from alternative asset management to ecology, philanthropy and environmental regeneration, Wall explained how his financial background created a strong basis for improving existing nature asset frameworks. Wall went on to discuss the use of AI within nature bio-characteristic assesments, the future of sustainable approaches to data centers and, crucially, what epiphany led Wall to develop what he saw as the real asset thesis for nature conservation with return parity with other classes.

articles.title: How Has the Data Discussion Evolved Since the Proliferation of AI?
articles.summary: Attending the Communify Intelligence Experience in London, Leon Saunders Calvert, President and Managing Director, Economist Enterprise spoke to FinextraTV to provide insights into how approaches and perceptions towards data have changed. Saunders Calvert said that the importance of data has not changed, but how it can be used and applied has significantly evolved. He mentions many of the opportunities that have arisen since the growth in AI and how this has dramatically transformed the data discussion, and equally the task of sustaining trust and preventing hallucinations. He emphasised the crucial nature of data within decision making and suggested this should remain the basis for how AI is used and applied.

articles.title: Treasury and Liquidity: How Do Traditional Corporates and Modern Platforms Differ?
articles.summary: Ahead of accepting an award at the Adam Smiths Awards in London, Anika Williams, Head of Treasury and Customer Payments Operations, Zalando Payments and Galina Kersten, EMEA Head of EMEA Head of Tech and Fintech Sales, Deutsche Bank joined FinextraTV. Williams began by contextualising the main differences between traditional corporate approaches to liquidity management and those of more modern digital platforms. She disagreed with the idea of these functions being 'back office operations' and explained why it is important to build treasury into the strategic planning for real growth. Kersten outlined a future of fintech firms and e-commerce platforms where a convergence will continue to grow as lines blur and each become much like the other - and both consider what this means for the future digital business in Europe.

articles.title: Why Verification Is a Critical Bridge Against Fraud, but Not a Silver Bullet
articles.summary: Taking time out of EBAday 2026, Jonathan Cardwell, Business Development Lead at Banfico, joined FinextraTV to discuss the necessary strategies to make fraud verification a success. Cardwell began by explaining where Verification works particularly well, but also where it struggles to properly combat fraud to the nature of authorise push payment fraud - namely, that it's authorised by a verified person. He described the need to add friction into the process on a risk-based approach, to avoid too much disruption to customer experience. He describes verification, not as a silver bullet but as a critical bridge between fraud prevention and fraud detection.

articles.title: How to Provide Optionality and Transparency for the Modern Customer
articles.summary: Joining the EBAday FinextraTV studio, Philip Konopik, SVP, Head of Commercial and Money Movement Solutions, Visa Europe, provided insights into the need for speed and flexibility for the modern customer. Konopik explained how building infrastructure is about creating optionality and 'stitching together network to network' in order to provide the best solutions for clients. Konopik described transparency as the most critical point within money movement, categorising it as foundational rather than hygienic. articles.summary: Die Banque Cantonale Neuchâteloise (BCN) hat im ersten Halbjahr 2026 operativ wieder zugelegt. Trotz des tiefen Zinsniveaus stieg der Geschäftserfolg um 6,3 Prozent auf 41,4 Millionen Franken. Unter dem Strich blieb der Halbjahresgewinn mit 24,1 Millionen Franken praktisch unverändert.
